en: Doors for a cash flow goal
Analyse every deal and run your offers from first look to closing
Deal analysis, offers, due diligence and loan quotes for real estate investors
Rental analyser with cap rate and DSCR
price, rent, costs and loan terms become NOI, cap rate, cash flow, cash-on-cash return and DSCR with a check against your targets
purchase, rehab, ARV and months to sell give the profit, the return and a pass or fail on the 70% rule
Maximum offer price for rentals and flips
the highest price that still reaches your return, worked back from rent, costs and loan terms, or from the ARV and the profit you want
five years of cash flow, the sale, the equity multiple and the IRR with rent, cost and value growth you choose
Offer ladder against the asking price
three offers at three discounts, each with its cash-on-cash return and DSCR, so you know how low to start and how high to go
Deal scorecard with your own weights
return, risk, location and rehab scored and weighted into one number with a Go, Review or No-go decision
Due diligence tracker with overdue alerts
every check before closing with its due date, the date it was done and a flag for what is late or due soon
lender, rate, points and term become the monthly payment and the cash to close, so quotes compare side by side
deals analysed and deals bought for each source show where your best deals come from
every deal with its offer share of asking, gross yield, cash needed and a flag for deals waiting too long for a decision

Every deal analysed, with offer, yield and cash needed
One row for each deal you look at; the offer share of asking, the total cost, the gross yield (yearly rent divided by price plus rehab), the cash needed and a decision flag fill in.
Offer as a share of asking
Total cost with closing and rehab
Offers with counters, accepted price and the gap to asking
One row for each offer with the counter-offer and the price both sides agreed; the address, the days from the deal to the offer, the gap to asking and the offer flag fill in.
Gap as a share of asking
Rental analyses with cap rate, cash-on-cash and DSCR
One row for each rental you underwrite; NOI (rent collected minus operating costs, before loan payments), cap rate, cash flow, cash-on-cash return and DSCR fill in.
Flip analyses with the 70% rule, profit and return
One row for each flip you underwrite; the highest offer under the 70% rule (offer at most 70% of the ARV minus the rehab), the profit and the return fill in.
Sales comparables with the price for each bedroom
One row for each recent sale near a deal with the bedrooms, the sold price and the sold date; the price for each bedroom and the age of the sale fill in.
Rental comparables with the rent for each bedroom
One row for each comparable rental with the bedrooms, the rent and the date it was listed; the rent for each bedroom and the days since it was listed fill in.
Rehab estimates by category with contingency
One row for each part of the work with the estimate and a contingency (a reserve for surprises); the address and the total with contingency fill in, so the rehab budget adds up before you offer.
Due diligence items with due dates and overdue flags
One row for each check before closing with the due date and the date it was done; the address, the timing flag and the days late fill in, so an item left open past its date stands out.
Inspections with issues found and the repair estimate
One row for each inspection with the issues and the repair estimate; the repair share of the price and a repair flag fill in, so a costly report can reopen the price.
Repairs as a share of the price
Loan quotes with the payment and the cash to close
One row for each lender quote (a balloon loan has its remaining balance due on one date); the loan, the monthly payment and the cash to close fill in, so quotes compare side by side.
Follow-ups with due dates and an overdue flag
One row for each task to move a deal forward with the owner and the due date; the address, the days to the due date and the flag fill in, so a late call to the seller stands out.
The 16 properties of the portfolio with the price, the closing costs and the rehab; the total cost and the gain against the value now fill in, so new deals are measured against what you hold.
The fees of a purchase, each a share of the price or a fixed amount; the Closing costs calculator adds them up, and the cost of each fee at your average offer fills in.
The ten numbers every analysis starts from; the same values sit in Start, so change them there and read them here.
Market rent by town and bedrooms
The market rent and the vacancy for each town and bedroom count; the rent for each bedroom fills in, so you can test a deal rent against the market.
Deal sources with the deals that closed
The six ways deals reach you with the deals analysed and the deals bought, so you see which source is worth your time.
Pass reasons with the number of deals
The reasons a deal was passed with the number of deals and a note, so you see what to fix in your buy box.
Pipeline stages with the target days and the deals now
The stages of the pipeline for holds and flips with the days each should take; the deals now at each stage and their asking value fill in from Deals.
Towns and their property tax rate
The towns you buy in with the yearly property tax as a share of the value.
The owner investor, the assistant and the ten outside contacts (agent, broker, contractors, manager, accountant, adviser, inspector, closing coordinator) with phone and rate.

Type the price, costs, rent and loan terms; see the NOI (rent collected minus operating costs, before loan payments), the cap rate, the cash flow, the cash-on-cash return and the DSCR.
Loan as a share of the price
Cap rate (NOI divided by price plus rehab)
Cash-on-cash return (cash flow divided by cash put in)
Flip deal analyser with the 70% rule
Type the purchase, the rehab, the ARV (the value after the work), the months and the costs; see the profit, the return and the 70% rule check (offer at most 70% of the ARV minus the rehab).
ARV, the value after the work
Selling costs as a share of the ARV
Holding cost a month (loan interest, tax, utilities)
Type the rent, the costs, the loan terms and the cash-on-cash return you want; see the highest price that still reaches it, the cash needed at that price and how it compares with the asking price.
Loan payments for each unit borrowed
Asking price minus the highest price
Highest price as a share of asking
Type the ARV, the rehab, the 70% rule and the profit you want; see the highest offer by the rule, the highest offer for your profit, the lower of the two and how the asking price compares.
Share of the ARV allowed (the 70% rule)
Asking price minus the highest offer
Highest offer as a share of asking
Type the price, the loan and the points; see the closing costs built from your Closing cost schedule, the points and the cash to close.
Points (a fee as a share of the loan)
Costs that are a share of the price
Quick estimate at your closing share
Loan payment and cash to close
Type the price, the loan share, the rate, the term and the points; see the monthly payment, the interest in the first year, the balance after five years and the cash you need to close.
Closing costs at your closing share
Type the rent and the bedrooms of three rental comparables and the bedrooms of the property; see each rent adjusted for the bedroom difference, the range and the rent to underwrite.
Planned rent minus the middle rent
Value estimate from three comparable sales
Type the sold price and the bedrooms of three comparable sales and the bedrooms of the property; see each price adjusted for the bedroom difference, the value range and how the asking price compares.
Asking price minus the middle value
Rehab quick budget by area and scope
Type the area, the scope level (1 light, 2 medium, 3 heavy), the cost for each area at each level and the contingency; see the budget, the cost for each area and the share of the ARV.
Cost for each area at your level
Budget for each area with contingency
Rehab as a share of the ARV
Type the deal and the growth; see five years of cash flow, the sale, the equity multiple and the IRR (the yearly return counting the timing of cash). Check with your own adviser.
Selling costs as a share of the sale price
Net cash from the sale after the loan
Total cash back over five years
Equity multiple (cash back divided by cash in)
Type the rent of a full building, the fixed costs, the loan payments and the units; see the share of units that must be rented to pay everything and how far you are above it.
Monthly rent when every unit is rented
Fixed costs for a year (tax, insurance, utilities)
Share of rent kept after management and repairs
Offer ladder: three offers against the asking price
Type the asking price, three discounts and the deal terms; see the offer, the cash-on-cash return and the DSCR for each step, so you know how far you can bid and how low you must start.
What-if grid: cash-on-cash by price and rent
Type the deal terms, then read the grid: each row shows the cash-on-cash return, the cash flow and the DSCR for one price and one rent, so you see which pairs reach your target.
Score the deal from 0 to 10 for return, risk, location and rehab, set the weight of each and the scores for Go and Review; see the weighted score and the decision.
Agent: a new deal matches the buy box
Hello, the deal at {address} with an asking price of {asking_price} matches our buy box. Please send the seller details and a viewing date.
Hello, please send comparable sales for {address} from the last 12 months. We need them for the analysis.
Agent: our offer for the property
Hello, our offer for {address} is {offer_price}, open until {valid_until}. The asking price was {asking_price}.
Hello, we accept the counter-offer for {address} at {final_price}. Please send the contract to the closing coordinator.
Agent: we are passing on the property
Hello, we are passing on {address}. The numbers do not meet our target. Thank you for your time, please keep sending deals.
Agent: ask for the seller repair credit
Hello, the inspection of {address} found repairs of {repair_estimate}. Please ask the seller for a credit or a lower price.
Loan broker: please quote a loan
Hello, please quote a loan for {address}: price {offer_price}, rehab {rehab_budget}. We need the rate, the points and the cash to close.
Loan broker: compare the two quotes
Hello, we are comparing quotes for {address}. Please confirm the monthly payment of {payment} and the cash to close of {cash_to_close} in writing.
Loan broker: the appraisal came in low
Hello, the appraisal for {address} came in below the price. Please tell us what the lender will lend now. The cash to close was {cash_to_close}.
Hello, we are sending the documents for the loan application for {address}. Please tell us what is still missing.
Hello, please book the inspection of {address} for {date}. Please send the report within two days.
Hello, please send the report summary for {address}. We need the {issues_found} issues with a cost for each.
Inspector: the repair estimate is needed
Hello, please add a repair estimate to the report for {address}. Our own estimate is {repair_estimate}.
Contractor: walk the property, price it
Hello, please walk {address} and price the {category} work. Our estimate is {estimate}.
General contractor: the bid is due
Hello, your bid for {address} is due. Please send the price for {category}. Our estimate with contingency is {total_with_cont}.
Hello, our offer on {address} was accepted at {final_price}. Please open the closing file.
